findings.condition: Native ERC found 5 errors: power_pin_not_driven on hidden GND pin of #PWR01 (36.83,78.74), on A1 pin 8 VMOT (48.26,219.71), and on J2 pin 90 12V_IGN (293.37,173.99); pin_not_connected on A1 pin 2 ~{FLT} (38.1,224.79); pin_to_pin between J2 pins 40 and 41, both 'Power output' type on 5V_SENSOR_1.

findings.mechanism: The GND, 12V_MR_FUSE and 12V_KEY rails are sourced only through passive connector/fuse pins with no PWR_FLAG or power-output pin, so KiCad cannot confirm the rails are driven; the DRV8825 fault output is left floating with no no-connect marker; J2 defines two paralleled pins as power outputs which conflict when tied. Electrically the rails are externally sourced via J1 and the ~FLT output is open-drain, so these are predominantly formal violations, but they mask any future genuinely-undriven rail.
findings.reasoning: Confirmed native rule violations in the candidate schematic. Connectivity shows the flagged rails are fed from harness connector pins through F1, so no actual floating supply exists under stated use; the ~FLT output is a status output whose omission loses stepper-fault visibility but does not break bias or startup. Classified defect (tool-confirmed) at minor severity; remediable with PWR_FLAGs, a no-connect marker, and pin-type cleanup on the J2 module symbol. The 348 warnings (229 endpoint_off_grid, lib mismatches, 1 same_local_global_label, 2 multiple_net_names) are hygiene items consistent with the imported hellen-one/Simon libraries.
findings.title: ERC reports 5 native error-severity violations (undriven power inputs, unconnected ~FLT, paralleled power outputs)

findings.mechanism: Annular-width and padstack errors indicate drilled pads/vias whose copper ring or stack geometry falls below the configured minimum, risking breakout or unreliable plated connections at fabrication; starved thermal spokes risk poor solder joints or marginal zone connection on thermal-relief pads.
findings.reasoning: Error-severity counts are native tool evidence, so this is reported as a defect even though the individual item coordinates lie past the truncated portion of drc.json and could not be inspected. The starved_thermal subset may be an artifact of the as-saved zone fill (the check explicitly forbade a refill pass), but annular-width/padstack errors are fill-independent and fabrication-relevant. Exact nets/locations need the full drc.json to disposition; severity major because annular/padstack errors can gate manufacturing.
findings.title: DRC reports 13 error-severity board violations: 5 padstack, 5 annular_width, 3 starved_thermal

findings.condition: The single sheet's 120R termination resistor is marked (dnp yes)/(in_bom no), so both hierarchy instances (R36 and R37) are DNP. The /CAN2+ and /CAN2- bus carries both wideband controllers (U1/U2 via U20/U21) and is also brought out on J1 pins 15/11 and J2 pins 73/74.

evidence.locator: symbol Device:R uuid d69380f9-5487-4782-9ce9-0690df62e543, Value '120', '(in_bom no)…(dnp yes)', instances R36 (/2889b04e…) and R37 (/10870bd0…)
footprint R36 dnp:true, pads on /CAN2+ and /CAN2- near (175.0,142.1)

findings.mechanism: With both terminations unpopulated, the internal CAN2 segment between the two TJA1051T-3 transceivers and the Polygonus module has no differential termination unless the builder populates R36/R37 or supplies external termination on the harness. An unterminated or singly-terminated high-speed CAN bus suffers reflections and bit errors, degrading or breaking wideband communication the README describes as internal to CAN bus #2.
findings.reasoning: Placement of the two 120R resistors near the two transceivers (x~81.6 and x~175.0) is a correct two-end termination scheme when both are populated (60R differential). Defaulting both to DNP is plausibly intentional because the bus is exposed on J1 for external extension, so termination choice is deferred to the builder; but nothing in the packet documents that, and the stated scope highlights 'internal dual-wideband CAN termination'. Labeled a concern, not a defect, since the DNP state may be a deliberate build option rather than an error.
findings.title: Both CAN2 120R termination resistors (R36, R37) are DNP; internal wideband bus unterminated as saved

findings.condition: Per the netlist, '/CRANK +' (J1.59) feeds R25 then R27 into U10 pin 2 (IN-), while '/CRANK -' (J1.55) feeds R26 then R28 into U10 pin 1 (IN+). The connector-positive signal lands on the inverting input and vice versa.

evidence.locator: U10 pads 1/2 on Net-(U10-IN+)/Net-(U10-IN-); R27/R28 pad nets consistent

findings.location: VR Conditioner sheet (/76f66c7e-94ea-4f9a-aa2e-a01725934e38/), U10 with R25-R28
findings.mechanism: For a VR zero-cross conditioner, swapping the differential inputs inverts the output edge relative to the sensor's true-zero crossing direction, which shifts which tooth edge the ECU triggers on. If firmware or documentation assumes the conventional VR+ -> IN+ mapping, crank timing edge selection would be inverted.
findings.reasoning: The input network itself (series 4.7k pairs, 1n differential C23, DNP attenuator/hysteresis options R29/R32/R33, BIAS at mid-rail via R30/R31/C24, pull-up R34 on the output) matches a standard MAX9924 differential VR application; only the +/- assignment relative to the connector labels is reversed. This is frequently an intentional edge-polarity choice (or the harness labels are arbitrary), and firmware can select the trigger edge, so it is a concern to confirm against FOME conventions rather than an evidence-proven defect. The symbol is from the custom 'Simon' library and the MAX9924 pin names come from the netlist labels; no datasheet was available in the packet to independently confirm pin 1/2 identity.
findings.title: CRANK+ / CRANK- connector signals arrive inverted at the MAX9924 differential inputs

findings.mechanism: All 107 Polygonus module pins (power, CAN, all I/O) route through J2. If the substituted footprint's pad numbering or geometry differed from the symbol's intended footprint, every module connection would be at risk. The parity check only compares footprint names/fields, not pad-to-pin compatibility.
findings.reasoning: The board netlist shows J2 pads carrying the expected nets and DRC reports 0 unconnected items, which indicates the substituted footprint's pad numbers do map to the schematic pins, so this is most likely a deliberate variant footprint (adding USB/SWD features). Marked a concern rather than a defect: pad-number mapping is validated by connectivity, but mechanical/geometric compatibility with the actual Polygonus module could not be verified from the packet.
findings.title: J2 module footprint on the board differs from the schematic symbol's footprint

findings.condition: Nets '/CAN+' [J1.47, J2.93] and '/CAN-' [J1.46, J2.94] contain only the harness connector and the module header: no NUP2105L clamp, no 47p filter caps, and no termination option, in contrast to the CAN2 bus which has all three.

evidence.locator: nets '/CAN+':[J1.47,J2.93] and '/CAN-':[J1.46,J2.94] vs '/CAN2+'/'/CAN2-' containing D10/D11 (NUP2105L) and C29/C30/C33/C34

findings.mechanism: If the Polygonus brain module does not carry its own CAN1 ESD protection, the primary vehicle CAN bus would be exposed to automotive transients directly at the module transceiver; absence of any base-board termination option also forces termination entirely into the harness.
findings.reasoning: This is consistent with the declared modular architecture: the CAN1 transceiver lives on the Polygonus module, which may include its own protection and termination, and the donor review explicitly excludes integrated module coverage and automotive transient qualification. Reported as an informational concern so the asymmetry versus CAN2 is dispositioned deliberately rather than by omission.
findings.title: CAN1 lines pass from module to harness with no on-board ESD protection, filtering or termination
